title: Dutch far-right activist Eva Vlaardingerbroek appears to lose right to UK visa-free travel
summary: Influencer, who promotes conspiracy theories and anti-immigration rhetoric, posts notification that her ETA has been cancelled A Dutch anti-immigration influencer who has promoted conspiracy theories such as the “great replacement” appears to have had her authorisation for visa-free travel to the UK revoked. Eva Vlaardingerbroek posted an image online of what appeared to be a notification from the British government that her UK electronic travel authorisation (ETA) had been cancelled on Tuesday. title: Ian McKellen to star as LS Lowry in documentary revealing trove of unheard tapes
summary: Exclusive: Artist reminisces about his life in film using interviews recorded in last four years of his life Fifteen years ago, Sir Ian McKellen was among the leading arts figures who criticised the Tate for not showing its collection of paintings by LS Lowry in its London galleries and questioned whether the “matchstick men painter” had been sidelined as too northern and provincial. Now, 50 years after Lowry’s death, McKellen is to star in a BBC documentary that will reveal a trove of previously unheard audio tapes recorded with Lowry in the 1970s during his final four years of life. title: US appeals court reverses decision that freed Mahmoud Khalil from ICE detention
summary: Ruling delivers victory to Trump administration in its efforts to deport the pro-Palestinian activist A federal appeals court on Thursday reversed a lower court decision that ordered the release of former Columbia University graduate student Mahmoud Khalil from immigration detention, delivering Donald Trump’s administration a victory in its efforts to deport the pro-Palestinian activist. A 2-1 panel of the Philadelphia-based third US circuit court of appeals ordered the dismissal of a lawsuit Khalil filed challenging his detention after finding that federal immigration law stripped the lower-court of jurisdiction over his claims. title: More Democratic lawmakers say Trump DoJ is investigating them over military video
summary: Three House members claim they’re being targeted for saying that troops don’t need to comply with illegal orders Three House Democrats confirmed Wednesday they have been approached by federal prosecutors investigating their participation in a November video about military duty, widening the circle of legislators being targeted by the Trump administration. Representatives Jason Crow of Colorado, Maggie Goodlander of New Hampshire, and Chrissy Houlahan of Pennsylvania disclosed on Wednesday that the US attorney’s office for the District of Columbia, led by Jeanine Pirro, had requested interviews about the 90-second video in which they said troops don’t need to comply with illegal orders.
